name: clinical-triage
description: The fairness-dimension taxonomy for clinical triage and prioritisation models that rank patients by clinical need.

dimensions.rationale: A ranking model that is miscalibrated for one group converts an accuracy gap into a harm gap, so calibration must be reported per group rather than in aggregate.
A per-group figure is meaningless without the cohort it was measured on, including the records excluded for missing inputs.
Differential missingness inflates apparent fairness, so the exclusion rate must be published per group.
A threshold that silently drops small groups makes the model unaudited for exactly the patients with the least data behind them.
Point estimates overstate certainty; overlapping intervals mean an apparent ordering between groups is not a finding.
An advisory ranking is only as fair as the workflow that consumes it, so the sign-off requirement is part of the fairness claim.
Excluding a protected attribute from the feature list does not exclude it from the prediction; proxy behaviour must be measured.
Training on records whose lawful basis cannot be reconstructed is a governance failure independent of model behaviour.
Retention is a governance obligation rather than a fairness property, so it is tracked but does not block attestation on its own.
